- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid over-optimistic spikes after recent highs; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.5 in 3–5 days), reduce forecast slope to avoid lagged overshoot.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias and adjust next forecast down 1–2%.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.30+ swings), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
